glance.label: Main Idea
glance.html: The priestly garments are made “as the LORD had commanded Moses,” the finished work of the tabernacle is brought to Moses, and he sees that everything has been done just as the LORD commanded and blesses the people.

glance.label: Setting
glance.html: Exodus 39 completes the building account of chapters 35–39. Its garment account follows the instructions of chapter 28, and only the setting up of the tabernacle in chapter 40 remains.

glance.label: Chapter Outline
glance.html:
• Exodus 39:1–7 — The Ephod and Its Memorial Stones

  • Exodus 39:8–21 — The Breastplate with Twelve Stones

  • Exodus 39:22–26 — The Blue Robe with Bells and Pomegranates

  • Exodus 39:27–31 — The Tunics, Turban, Sash, and Holy Crown

  • Exodus 39:32–43 — The Finished Work Is Brought to Moses and He Blesses the People

glance.label: Key Verse
glance.html: “Then Moses looked over all the work, and indeed they had done it; as the LORD had commanded, just so they had done it. And Moses blessed them.” (Exodus 39:43)

cards.title: The Heart of the Chapter
cards.html:
The workers make the holy garments for Aaron, and after each one the same words return: “as the LORD had commanded Moses” (39:1). The phrase sounds seven times through the garment account. The ephod is woven with threads of beaten gold, and on its shoulders sit the onyx stones bearing the names of Israel’s sons. The breastplate holds twelve stones, one for each tribe, fastened securely over the place where Aaron’s heart will be. The blue robe is hemmed with golden bells and pomegranates, and the gold plate reads HOLINESS TO THE LORD. Not long before, Aaron had made a calf at the people’s demand. Now the garments for his priestly service are made exactly according to the LORD’s word.

Then the people bring everything to Moses: the tent and its frame, the coverings, the veil, the ark and mercy seat, the table and bread, the lampstand, the altars, the laver, the courtyard, and the priests’ garments. Nothing is missing. Moses looks over the whole work, “and indeed they had done it; as the LORD had commanded, just so they had done it. And Moses blessed them” (39:43). The scene recalls God looking over His finished creation and blessing it. Everything is ready. All that remains is for the tabernacle to be raised and for God to come.

cards.title: Chapter Sections
cards.html:
Exodus 39:1–7 — The Ephod and Its Memorial Stones

The workers make the holy garments for Aaron from blue, purple, and scarlet thread, weaving the ephod with threads of beaten gold. Onyx stones engraved with the names of Israel’s sons are set on its shoulders as memorial stones, as the LORD commanded Moses.

Exodus 39:8–21 — The Breastplate with Twelve Stones

The breastplate is woven square and set with four rows of precious stones, twelve in all, engraved with the names of Israel’s tribes. It is fastened to the ephod with gold chains, rings, and a blue cord so that it will not come loose.

Exodus 39:22–26 — The Blue Robe with Bells and Pomegranates

The robe of the ephod is woven all of blue, with a strong opening for the head. Its hem carries pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn alternating with bells of pure gold all the way around.

Exodus 39:27–31 — The Tunics, Turban, Sash, and Holy Crown

Linen tunics, a turban, caps, undergarments, and a sash are made for Aaron and his sons. The plate of the holy crown is made of pure gold, engraved HOLINESS TO THE LORD, and fastened to the turban with a blue cord.

Exodus 39:32–43 — The Finished Work Is Brought to Moses and He Blesses the People

All the work of the tabernacle is finished, and the people bring Moses the tent with its furnishings, the courtyard, and the priests’ garments. Moses inspects everything, sees that it has been done exactly as the LORD commanded, and blesses them.

cards.title: Why This Chapter Matters
cards.html:
Exodus 39 shows what obedience looks like after failure. The people who had made a calf now did “all the work” according to God’s command (39:42). Their obedience did not earn God’s presence, but it prepared a place for Him, and Moses’ blessing honored their faithful work.

The garments carry forward the picture of the high priest who bears his people’s names on his shoulders and over his heart. That picture finds its fulfillment in Jesus, the High Priest who carries His people before the Father. The chapter also shows the joy of finished work done God’s way: everything ready, nothing left out, and the workers blessed.

cards.title: Key Themes to Watch For
cards.html:
As the LORD commanded. The refrain marks every stage of the work as obedience (39:1, 5, 7, 21, 26, 29, 31, 42).

Names carried before God. Israel’s names are set on the shoulders and over the heart of the high priest (39:6–7, 14).

Holiness to the LORD. The gold plate marks the high priest as set apart to God (39:30).

The work completed. Every part of the tabernacle is finished and brought to Moses (39:32–41).

Blessing for faithful work. Moses inspects the work and blesses the people (39:43).

cards.title: Key Words & Concepts
cards.html:
Ephod (39:2). The high priest’s outer garment, woven with gold threads and bearing two onyx stones on its shoulders.

Memorial stones (39:7). The engraved onyx stones that kept Israel’s names before the LORD.

Breastplate (39:8). The square pouch over the high priest’s chest, set with twelve stones for the tribes.

Holy crown (39:30). The gold plate engraved HOLINESS TO THE LORD, fastened to the front of the turban.

Tent of meeting (39:32). Another name for the tabernacle, the place where God would meet with His people.

focus: Exodus 39 records the making of the priestly garments, the ephod, breastplate, robe, tunics, and the gold plate, each made “as the LORD had commanded Moses” (Exodus 39:1). The finished work of the tabernacle is then brought to Moses, who sees that everything was done just as the LORD commanded and blesses the people.

sections.title: The Ephod and Its Memorial Stones
sections.summary: The holy garments for Aaron are made of blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and the ephod is woven with gold beaten into threads. Onyx stones engraved with the names of the sons of Israel are set on its shoulders “as memorial stones for the sons of Israel” (Exodus 39:7).

sections.title: The Breastplate with Twelve Stones
sections.summary: The breastplate is woven square and set with four rows of stones, “twelve stones according to the names of the sons of Israel” (Exodus 39:14). It is fastened to the ephod with gold chains, rings, and a blue cord so that it will not come loose.

sections.title: The Blue Robe with Bells and Pomegranates
sections.summary: The robe of the ephod is woven all of blue, with a reinforced opening for the head. Its hem carries pomegranates and bells of pure gold, “a bell and a pomegranate” (Exodus 39:26) all around.

sections.title: The Tunics, Turban, Sash, and Holy Crown
sections.summary: Tunics, a turban, hats, trousers, and a sash are made of fine linen for Aaron and his sons. The plate of the holy crown is made of pure gold, engraved HOLINESS TO THE LORD, and tied with a blue cord to the turban.

sections.title: The Finished Work Is Brought to Moses and He Blesses the People
sections.summary: All the work of the tabernacle is finished, and the people bring Moses the tent with all its furnishings, the courtyard, and the priestly garments. Moses looks over the work and sees that “as the LORD had commanded, just so they had done it” (Exodus 39:43), and he blesses them.

1.brief: From blue, purple, and scarlet thread the workers make garments for ministering in the holy place and the holy garments for Aaron, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” The refrain of obedience that runs through the chapter begins.
1.explain:
“Of the blue, purple, and scarlet thread they made garments of ministry, for ministering in the holy place,”

The workers make “garments of ministry,” clothing for service in the holy place.

“and made the holy garments for Aaron, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

They make Aaron’s “holy garments” “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” This phrase returns seven times in the garment account (39:1, 5, 7, 21, 26, 29, 31). Aaron had made the calf according to the people’s demand (32:1–5). Now the garments for his priestly service are made according to the LORD’s word.
1.notes: Exodus 39:1–31 records the making of the garments described in 28:1–43. The explanations given there apply here.

2.brief: Bezalel makes the ephod of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine woven linen. The high priest’s chief garment is made.
2.explain:
“He made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and of fine woven linen.”

The high priest’s chief garment is made (28:6).

3.brief: The workers beat gold into thin sheets and cut it into threads to weave into the fabric. Gold is woven into the very cloth.
3.explain:
“And they beat the gold into thin sheets and cut it into threads,”

This detail is new. The workers hammer gold into “thin sheets” and cut it into “threads.”

“to work it in with the blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and the fine linen, into artistic designs.”

The gold is woven into the fabric itself.

4.brief: The workers make shoulder straps for the ephod, joined at its two edges. The shoulders that will carry the names are prepared.
4.explain:
“They made shoulder straps for it to couple it together; it was coupled together at its two edges.”

The shoulders that will carry the names are prepared (28:7).

5.brief: The woven band of the ephod is made of the same materials, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” The workmanship matches God’s instructions.
5.explain:
“And the intricately woven band of his ephod that was on it was of the same workmanship,”

The band matches the ephod (28:8).

“woven of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and of fine woven linen, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

The refrain of obedience returns.

6.brief: The workers set onyx stones in gold settings, engraved like signets with the names of the sons of Israel. The tribes’ names are permanently engraved.
6.explain:
“And they set onyx stones, enclosed in settings of gold;”

The onyx stones are set in gold (28:9–11).

“they were engraved, as signets are engraved, with the names of the sons of Israel.”

The tribes’ names are permanently engraved.

7.brief: The stones are put on the shoulders of the ephod as memorial stones for Israel, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” Aaron will carry the people before God on his shoulders.
7.explain:
“He put them on the shoulders of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

The stones go on the shoulders “as memorial stones” (28:12). Aaron will carry the people before God on his shoulders.

8.brief: Bezalel makes the breastplate, woven like the ephod of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen. The breastplate is made.
8.explain:
“And he made the breastplate, artistically woven like the workmanship of the ephod, of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and of fine woven linen.”

The breastplate is made (28:15).

9.brief: The workers double the breastplate into a square, a span long and wide. The breastplate takes its proper shape.
9.explain:
“They made the breastplate square by doubling it; a span was its length and a span its width when doubled.”

It is doubled into a square pouch (28:16).

10.brief: The workers set in it four rows of stones, the first a sardius, a topaz, and an emerald. The precious stones are mounted.
10.explain:
“And they set in it four rows of stones: a row with a sardius, a topaz, and an emerald was the first row;”

The four rows of stones are mounted (28:17).

11.brief: The second row is a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond. The rows continue as God described.
11.explain:
“the second row, a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;”

The second row follows (28:18).

12.brief: The third row is a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst. Each row is completed.
12.explain:
“the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;”

The third row follows (28:19).

13.brief: The fourth row is a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper, all set in gold. Twelve stones are in place.
13.explain:
“the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper.”

The fourth row completes the twelve (28:20).

“They were enclosed in settings of gold in their mountings.”

All are set in gold.

14.brief: The twelve stones are engraved like signets with the names of the twelve tribes. Each tribe is individually remembered over Aaron’s heart.
14.explain:
“There were twelve stones according to the names of the sons of Israel:”

Each of the “twelve stones” bears a tribe’s name.

“according to their names, engraved like a signet, each one with its own name according to the twelve tribes.”

Each tribe is individually remembered over Aaron’s heart (28:21, 29).

15.brief: The workers make chains of pure gold like braided cords for the breastplate. The breastplate is prepared for fastening.
15.explain:
“And they made chains for the breastplate at the ends, like braided cords of pure gold.”

Two chains of pure gold, twisted like braided cords, are made for the breastplate. They will hang from the shoulder straps and hold the breastplate up on the high priest’s chest (28:22).

16.brief: The workers make two gold settings and two gold rings and put the rings on the two ends of the breastplate. The attachments are made.
16.explain:
“They also made two settings of gold and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.”

Two gold settings are made to attach to the shoulder straps, and two gold rings are fastened at the two upper ends of the breastplate (28:23, 25).

17.brief: The workers put the two gold chains in the rings on the ends of the breastplate. The breastplate is linked.
17.explain:
“And they put the two braided chains of gold in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate.”

Each chain passes through one of these rings, so the upper corners of the breastplate hang from the chains (28:24).

18.brief: The workers fasten the other ends of the chains to the settings on the shoulder straps in front. Shoulders and heart are joined.
18.explain:
“The two ends of the two braided chains they fastened in the two settings, and put them on the shoulder straps of the ephod in the front.”

The other end of each chain is fastened to a gold setting on the front of a shoulder strap (28:25). The breastplate now hangs from the shoulders, linking the names carried on the shoulders with the names worn over the heart. Shoulders and heart are joined.

19.brief: The workers make two gold rings for the inner edge of the breastplate. The lower edge is secured.
19.explain:
“And they made two rings of gold and put them on the two ends of the breastplate, on the edge of it, which was on the inward side of the ephod.”

Two more rings are fixed at the lower corners of the breastplate, on its inner edge, the side that lies against the ephod (28:26). They will hold the bottom of the breastplate in place.

20.brief: The workers make two other gold rings on the shoulder straps below, at the seam above the band. The fittings are completed.
20.explain:
“They made two other gold rings and put them on the two shoulder straps, underneath the ephod toward its front, right at the seam above the intricately woven band of the ephod.”

Matching rings are set low on the front of the shoulder straps, just above the woven band of the ephod (28:27). The next verse explains that a blue cord ties the breastplate’s lower rings to these rings, so the breastplate does not come loose from the ephod (39:21).

21.brief: The workers tie the breastplate to the ephod with a blue cord so it does not come loose, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” The names over Aaron’s heart are fixed securely.
21.explain:
“And they bound the breastplate by means of its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord,”

A “blue cord” ties the breastplate in place (28:28).

“so that it would be above the intricately woven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate would not come loose from the ephod, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

The breastplate cannot come loose. The names over Aaron’s heart are fixed securely.

22.brief: Bezalel makes the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of blue. The robe is made.
22.explain:
“He made the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of blue.”

The blue robe is made (28:31).

23.brief: The robe has an opening in the middle with a woven binding so it will not tear. Its finish follows God’s instructions.
23.explain:
“And there was an opening in the middle of the robe, like the opening in a coat of mail, with a woven binding all around the opening, so that it would not tear.”

Its neck is reinforced (28:32).

24.brief: The workers make pomegranates of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen on the hem of the robe. The hem is adorned.
24.explain:
“They made on the hem of the robe pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet, and of fine woven linen.”

Pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen are made for the hem of the robe of the ephod (28:33).

25.brief: The workers make bells of pure gold and put them between the pomegranates all around the hem. The bells are added.
25.explain:
“And they made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates on the hem of the robe all around between the pomegranates:”

Gold bells hang between the pomegranates all the way around the hem.

26.brief: A bell and a pomegranate alternate around the hem for ministering, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” The robe is completed as God said.
26.explain:
“a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe to minister in, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

Bell and pomegranate alternate all around the hem. The robe is worn “to minister in,” and its bells were to be heard when Aaron went into the holy place before the LORD and when he came out (28:35). The robe is completed as God said.

27.brief: The workers make woven tunics of fine linen for Aaron and his sons. The inner garments are made.
27.explain:
“They made tunics, artistically woven of fine linen, for Aaron and his sons,”

The linen tunics are made (28:39–40).

28.brief: The workers make a turban of fine linen, fine linen hats, and short trousers of fine woven linen. More of the priests’ linen garments are made.
28.explain:
“a turban of fine linen, exquisite hats of fine linen, short trousers of fine woven linen,”

The turban, hats, and trousers are made (28:39–42).

29.brief: The workers make a woven sash of fine linen with blue, purple, and scarlet, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” Every garment follows God’s instruction.
29.explain:
“and a sash of fine woven linen with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, made by a weaver, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

The sash completes the priestly garments. Every garment follows God’s instruction.

30.brief: The workers make the plate of the holy crown of pure gold and engrave on it, “HOLINESS TO THE LORD.” The declaration of consecration is made.
30.explain:
“Then they made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold,”

The gold “plate of the holy crown” is made (28:36).

“and wrote on it an inscription like the engraving of a signet: HOLINESS TO THE LORD.”

It bears the words HOLINESS TO THE LORD. The high priest is marked as consecrated to God, bearing the guilt of Israel’s holy gifts so that they may be accepted (28:38).

31.brief: The workers tie a blue cord to it to fasten it on the turban, “as the LORD had commanded Moses.” The garment account closes with the same refrain of obedience.
31.explain:
“And they tied to it a blue cord, to fasten it above on the turban, as the LORD had commanded Moses.”

The plate is fastened to the turban. The garment account closes with the same refrain of obedience. The garments’ priestly functions point toward Christ’s greater priesthood (Hebrews 7:26–28; 8:1–2).

32.brief: “Thus all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was finished,” and Israel did according to all that the LORD commanded Moses. The tabernacle work is complete, done just as the LORD commanded.
32.explain:
“Thus all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was finished.”

The construction is complete. “All the work” is “finished.”

“And the children of Israel did according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses; so they did.”

The whole people obeyed. The tabernacle work is complete, done just as the LORD commanded.

33.brief: The people bring the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, clasps, boards, bars, pillars, and sockets. The finished work is presented for inspection.
33.explain:
“And they brought the tabernacle to Moses, the tent and all its furnishings:”

The people bring the finished parts “to Moses” for inspection.

“its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;”

The list begins with the structure.

34.brief: The people bring the coverings of ram skins and badger skins and the veil of the covering. Every part of the tent is brought.
34.explain:
“the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of badger skins, and the veil of the covering;”

The coverings and the veil are presented.

35.brief: The people bring the ark of the Testimony with its poles and the mercy seat. The holiest furnishing is presented.
35.explain:
“the ark of the Testimony with its poles, and the mercy seat;”

The holiest furnishing is presented.

36.brief: The people bring the table, its utensils, and the showbread. The furnishings of the holy place follow.
36.explain:
“the table, all its utensils, and the showbread;”

The furnishings of the holy place follow.

37.brief: The people bring the pure gold lampstand with its lamps set in order, its utensils, and the oil for light. The light of the sanctuary is ready.
37.explain:
“the pure gold lampstand with its lamps (the lamps set in order), all its utensils, and the oil for light;”

The lampstand and its oil are ready.

38.brief: The people bring the gold altar, the anointing oil, the sweet incense, and the screen for the door. The supplies for worship are presented.
38.explain:
“the gold altar, the anointing oil, and the sweet incense; the screen for the tabernacle door;”

The supplies for worship are presented.

39.brief: The people bring the bronze altar with its grate, poles, and utensils, and the laver with its base. The courtyard furnishings are presented.
39.explain:
“the bronze altar, its grate of bronze, its poles, and all its utensils; the laver with its base;”

The courtyard furnishings are presented.

40.brief: The people bring the court’s hangings, pillars, sockets, gate screen, cords, and pegs, and all the utensils for the service of the tabernacle. Nothing is missing.
40.explain:
“the hangings of the court, its pillars and its sockets, the screen for the court gate, its cords, and its pegs;”

The courtyard enclosure is presented.

“all the utensils for the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;”

Nothing is missing.

41.brief: The people bring the garments of ministry, the holy garments for Aaron and his sons. Everything God commanded has been made.
41.explain:
“and the garments of ministry, to minister in the holy place: the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons’ garments, to minister as priests.”

The priestly garments complete the list. Everything God commanded has been made.

42.brief: “According to all that the LORD had commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did all the work.” The whole people carried out God’s pattern faithfully.
42.explain:
“According to all that the LORD had commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did all the work.”

The narrator states it once more. The whole people carried out God’s pattern faithfully.

43.brief: Moses looks over all the work and sees that “as the LORD had commanded, just so they had done it,” and he blesses them. The faithful work receives Moses’ approval and blessing.
43.explain:
“Then Moses looked over all the work, and indeed they had done it; as the LORD had commanded, just so they had done it.”

Moses “looked over all the work” and found it exactly as God commanded.

“And Moses blessed them.”

The blessing completes the scene, and the sequence recalls creation. God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. He finished His work and blessed the seventh day (Genesis 1:31–2:3). The faithful work receives Moses’ approval and blessing. The components are ready, but the tent still awaits assembly and the LORD’s glory in chapter 40.
